rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Parent-chain + locant(s) + sub-prefix + suffix = IUPAC name

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ treat "Classification of organic compounds" as one blob → ✅ split into: classification of organic compounds.  ·  ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: IUPAC: identify parent chain (longest), number from end nearer the functional group / first substituent; suffix by priority (−ol, −al, −one, −oic acid…).  ·  Carbocation/carbanion stability: 3° > 2° > 1° > methyl; resonance stabilises; inductive effect transmits through sigma bonds.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Open-chain compounds.** Aliphatic compounds have open carbon chains — straight-chain (n-butane) or branched-chain (isobutane) — and may be saturated or unsaturated.  ·  **Cyclic compounds.** Closed-ring compounds divide into carbocycles (alicyclic like cyclohexane; aromatic like benzene) and heterocycles (furan, pyridine) that contain non-carbon atoms in the ring.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Functional group priority (high → low) governs the suffix; others become prefixes with locants.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Functional group classes.** Compounds are grouped by their functional group: halides (—X), alcohols (—OH), aldehydes (—CHO), ketones (>C=O), carboxylic acids (—COOH) and amines (—NH₂).  ·  **Saturated vs unsaturated.** Compounds with only single C—C bonds are saturated; those with double or triple bonds are unsaturated and decolourise bromine water.  ·  **Why classification matters.** Members of one class show similar chemical properties, so classifying a compound immediately predicts its reactions and its name.
